_comment: Defaults for mos-geo-topic-clusters. Override per run with --config <file> (a partial JSON merged over this one). Values marked PLACEHOLDER are untuned: tune them on a labelled set of keyword pairs before trusting them. Nothing client-specific belongs here: brand terms, extra suburbs and country filters go in the per-run --config file or on the command line.

input._comment: Ahrefs exports list a keyword once per country, each with its own volume, position and URL. country: the Ahrefs Country code whose rows are used for demand, position and URL; null = the file's most common Country (printed by ingest); "all" keeps every country (demand then sums across countries, which mixes markets). volume_dedupe (sum, max or kept) only decides how rows that normalise to the same keyword combine.
input._gsc_comment: GSC lists jump links (/page/#section) as separate URLs. true merges them into the page so they don't count as cannibalisation.

brand._comment: Own-brand keywords are pulled out before clustering and reported on their own. terms: per-run brand names, misspellings and product names (pass --brand-terms). use_host: also treat a keyword as own-brand when, with spaces removed, it contains the site's host name without its TLD. use_ahrefs_flag: Ahrefs 'Branded' rows that are not own-brand (usually competitor or third-party brands) form their own walled partition.

local._comment: Local keywords never share a cluster with non-local ones. A keyword is local when the Ahrefs Local flag is set or it contains one of these terms or places as whole words. Add suburbs and regions per run with --config.

intent._comment: Used when the export carries no intent flags (GSC), or when Ahrefs flags are mixed. informational and commercial never share a cluster; mixed can join either. Words match as whole words on the normalised keyword.

embeddings._comment: Recall only: embeddings propose neighbour pairs, they never decide a cluster. Auto order: OPENAI_API_KEY first, then VOYAGE_API_KEY, then none (lexical + shared-URL recall only; the README warns that synonyms may be missed). Override with --embeddings openai|voyage|none. Vectors are cached on disk by (provider, model, dimensions, text).

recall._comment: Candidate pairs per anchor keyword. PLACEHOLDER floors: cos_floor is for 256-dimension text-embedding-3-small vectors of short queries; lex_min_jaccard is over stemmed content tokens. Pairs whose content tokens are identical (plurals, word order, 's) become same-page edges in code and never cost a Jev call.

jev._model_comment: Pin the versioned id the response 'model' field reports (e.g. jev-1.13.0) once thresholds are tuned; the alias moves.

thresholds._comment: PLACEHOLDER values: chosen by reading the first real runs, not tuned on labelled pairs. merge_min: average P(same-page) two groups need to merge. cannot_link_min_different: a pair Jev judges P(different) at or above this can never share a cluster. min_coverage: judged pairs needed between two groups, as a share of the smaller group's size, so one strong edge cannot chain two groups together. topic_min / topic_min_coverage: the same for rolling clusters up into topics, on P(related) + topic_same_weight x P(same-page) of judged pairs across two clusters. verify_min_cluster: clusters this size or larger get every member re-judged against the cluster head. singleton_min_demand: a keyword left alone becomes its own cluster (one page) at or above this demand, else it goes to Unclustered.

serp._comment: Optional, off by default (--serp stage). DataForSEO Google organic top 10, live endpoint. Uncertain edges (P(same-page) inside uncertain_band) are decided by shared URLs: >= merge_min_shared merges, < split_below splits, in between keeps Jev's answer. Cluster heads in the same topic that share >= merge_min_shared URLs are merged. Platform domains are removed before counting. location_code 2036 = Australia: override per run.

scoring._comment: All maths in code. PLACEHOLDER: cannibalisation rule from the research (second URL holds >= min share and sits within max_position_gap), ctr_curve is a generic organic CTR-by-position assumption used for the opportunity score on Ahrefs data (GSC uses its real CTR).
